verdict.rationale: Paddle's own docs describe inline checkout via Paddle.js, which embeds the checkout in your own interface rather than redirecting to a hosted page. An overlay checkout option also opens in-page. However, the evidence never describes what can be customized (styling, fields, branding controls); the 'branded' label appears only in a doc URL, so the 'customizable components' part of the story is thin. Missing for 10: documented customization options for the embedded components (theming, styling, layout, field control), independent or hands-on corroboration of the embedded checkout.

support.subject: As a developer, I can embed customizable payment components directly in my own site or app instead of redirecting to a hosted page

citations.quote: Inline checkout lets you embed a checkout and display information about items and totals in your own interface, creating checkout experiences that are fully integrated with your app.
Add a checkout to your app or website using Paddle.js to let customers buy one-time products and sign up for a subscriptions.
Overlay checkout lets you present customers with an overlay that handles all parts of the checkout process — minimal frontend coding required.
